# Two Seconds Of Isometric Hold Count As One Rep For SasaVenos

SasaVenos reports that he uses the conversion that two seconds of isometric hold equals one rep, which he applies to his maltese and cross training. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]

## Details

- He says that two seconds of isometric hold equals one rep. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- Using this conversion, his three seconds of max maltese hold is basically his one rep max. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- This means that when he was maxing out his three seconds of maltese and five seconds of cross every session, he was training in the 95 to 100 of his rep max. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]

## Evidence

- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "two seconds of isometric hold equals one rep so three seconds of max maltese hold is basically my one rep max so the whole time i'm training in the 95 to 100 of my rep max wondering what's wrong"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "maxing out my three seconds of maltese and five seconds of cross every single session wondering why i can't make any progress"

## Connected Ideas

- [[SasaVenos Recommends No More Than 30 To 40 Seconds Of Banded Skill Volume Per Session After His Own Maltese Trial]] — uses this conversion to define 80 to 90 percent rep max as 8 to 16 seconds.
